threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the tube' means a quick ride, not a gamble on whether you'll get stuck between stations for ages.
Last night on the 333, a guy pulled out a saxophone and just played Smooth Operator as we rolled past Windrush Square. Honestly, only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids playing football in the rain, laughing like it was summer. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you’ll find pop-up espresso bars on street corners, where baristas serve quality brews from bike carts. It's like a caffeine scavenger hunt!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows to keep an eye on BART delays before planning a trip to the East Bay; it's like checking the weather but way more chaotic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a guy serenading passengers with an out-of-tune ukulele. Only in SF do you get concert-like delays without extra fare.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell but miss the hidden gardens tucked behind Carrer de Fraternitat. That’s where the real charm lies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell them apart by how they still ask for milk in their coffee. Locals have fully embraced the cortado.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stand by the curb waiting for a non-existent taxi instead of flagging down an Uber like the rest of us.
Caught a chatty group on the 12 last night; one lad was convinced the bus drivers know all the best late-night food spots. He might be onto something!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Waking up to the sound of spontaneous parties on the street—every Saturday morning feels like a little festival of life.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find spontaneous raves in abandoned buildings with a full DJ setup, often just a text away from your friends.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's local when they dodge the BART delays and recommend the best taco shop, while the newcomers are still planning around the chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the 14 Muni while a woman serenaded him with an old soul tune. Only in SF do you get cabaret for your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all of Gràcia is the same, but the vibe changes at every plaza. Each one tells a different story—especially at night.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to try tapas at 11 PM. Locals know that's when the real socializing begins.
